```ruby
  def self.truncate(str, limit)
```

```ruby
class Counter
  def initialize
    @value = 0
    @step = 1
  end

  def value
    @value
  end

  def bump
    @value += @step
    self
  end

  def with_step(step)
    previous_step = @step
    begin
      @step = step
      yield
    ensure
      @step = previous_step
    end
  end

  def dup
    copy = self.class.new
    copy.instance_variable_set(:@value, @value)
    copy.instance_variable_set(:@step, @step)
    copy
  end

  def clone
    dup
  end
end
```

```ruby
class Proxy
  # Store the target object in a private accessor so we can forward calls to it.
  attr_reader :target

  # Factory method to create a Proxy wrapping the given target object.
  def self.new(target)
    obj = allocate
    obj.init(target)
    obj
  end

  # Initialize with a target object to wrap.
  def init(target)
    @target = target
  end

  # Forwards any method that the target responds to to the target.
  def method_missing(name, *args, **kwargs)
    if target.respond_to?(name)
      if kwargs.any?
        target.send(name, *args, **kwargs)
      else
        target.send(name, *args, **kwargs)
      end
    else
      super
    end
  end

  # Forwards respond_to? checks to the target as well.
  def respond_to?(name, include_all = false)
    if target.respond_to?(name, include_all)
      true
    else
      super(name, include_all)
    end
  end

  # Forwards method(:name) calls to the target if target responds to it,
  # otherwise delegates to super (which will raise NameError for unsupported methods).
  def method(name)
    if target.respond_to?(name)
      target.method(name)
    else
      super(name)
    end
  end
end
```

```ruby
class TransientError < StandardError; end
class PermanentError < StandardError; end

module Retrier
  def self.call(max_attempts:, &block)
    attempt_number = 0

    loop do
      attempt_number += 1

      if attempt_number >= max_attempts
        # Final attempt — if it raises TransientError, let it propagate
        result = block.call(attempt_number)
        return result
      else
        begin
          result = block.call(attempt_number)
          return result
        rescue TransientError => e
          # Retry if this was not the final attempt
          continue_attempt = true
          continue_attempt
        rescue PermanentError => e
          raise e
        end
      end
    end
  end
end
```

```ruby
class Ledger
  def initialize(entries = [])
    @entries = Array.new(entries)
    @frozen = false
  end

      raise FrozenError, "Cannot add entry to a frozen Ledger"

  end
```

```ruby
class TokenStream
  def initialize(tokens)
    @tokens = tokens
    @index = 0
  end

  def next
    if @index >= @tokens.length
      raise StopIteration
    end
    token = @tokens[@index]
    @index += 1
    token
  end

  def peek
    if @index >= @tokens.length
      raise StopIteration
    end
    @tokens[@index]
  end

  def rewind
    @index = 0
  end
end
```

Implement Weight.new(amount, unit), constructed with a numeric amount and a unit (any object identifying the unit, such as a Symbol like :kg or :lb), exposed unchanged via public #amount and #unit readers. Two Weights with the same unit order strictly by amount - Weight.new(5, :kg) is less than Weight.new(10, :kg) - and support sort, clamp, and between? accordingly whenever every Weight involved shares the same unit. Two Weights are == to each other only when both their unit and their amount are equal; two Weights with different units are never == to each other, even when their amounts happen to match. Comparing two Weights of different units with <, <=, >, or >=, sorting an array that mixes units, or calling clamp or between? with a bound of a different unit, raises ArgumentError rather than silently producing some ordering.

```ruby
class Weight
  attr_reader :amount, :unit

  def initialize(amount, unit)
    @amount = amount
    @unit = unit
  end

  def ==(other)
    return false unless other.is_a?(Weight)
    unit == other.unit && amount == other.amount
  end

  def <(other)
    unless other.is_a?(Weight) && unit == other.unit
      raise ArgumentError, "Cannot compare weights with different units"
    end
    amount < other.amount
  end

  def <=(other)
    unless other.is_a?(Weight) && unit == other.unit
      raise ArgumentError, "Cannot compare weights with different units"
    end
    amount <= other.amount
  end

  def >(other)
    unless other.is_a?(Weight) && unit == other.unit
      raise ArgumentError, "Cannot compare weights with different units"
    end
    amount > other.amount
  end

  def >=(other)
    unless other.is_a?(Weight) && unit == other.unit
      raise ArgumentError, "Cannot compare weights with different units"
    end
    amount >= other.amount
  end

  def <=>(other)
    unless other.is_a?(Weight)
      return nil
    end
    if unit != other.unit
      raise ArgumentError, "Cannot compare weights with different units"
    end
    amount <=> other.amount
  end

  def clamp(min, max)
    unless min.is_a?(Weight) && max.is_a?(Weight) && unit == min.unit && unit == max.unit
      raise ArgumentError, "Cannot clamp with bounds of different units"
    end
    if amount < min.amount
      self.class.new(min.amount, min.unit)
    elsif amount > max.amount
      self.class.new(max.amount, max.unit)
    else
      self
    end
  end

  def between?(min, max)
    unless min.is_a?(Weight) && max.is_a?(Weight) && unit == min.unit && unit == max.unit
      raise ArgumentError, "Cannot check between? with bounds of different units"
    end
    amount >= min.amount && amount <= max.amount
  end

  def hash
    [amount, unit].hash
  end

  def ==(other)
    return false unless other.is_a?(Weight)
    unit == other.unit && amount == other.amount
  end

  def ==(other)
    return false unless other.is_a?(Weight)
    unit == other.unit && amount == other.amount
  end

  def ==(other)
    return false unless other.is_a?(Weight)
```

```ruby
def Memoizer.wrap(&computation)
  if computation.nil?
    raise ArgumentError, "computation must be provided"
  end

  invoked = false
  result = nil

  ->(*args, **kwargs) {
    unless invoked
      result = computation(*args, **kwargs)
      invoked = true
    end

    result
  }
end
```

This must work correctly both with the default in-memory storage (packer: nil) and when constructed with a packer object such as Marshal (Cache.new(packer: Marshal)) - #write and every method that later inspects a stored entry must round-trip it through that packer (packer.dump when writing, packer.load when reading it back, whether for #read or for #sweep's own stale check).

message.content:
I'll analyze this task carefully.

**Key Requirements:**

1. `Cache.new(packer: nil)` - factory constructor that accepts `packer:` keyword argument. Calling `Cache.new(...)` should **not** invoke `#initialize` (which isn't defined), so I must override `new` on the metaclass.
2. `#write(key, payload, stale: false)` - stores payload under key; must persist the `stale` flag too.
3. `#read(key)` - returns most recently written payload, `nil` if never written or removed by `#sweep`.
4. `#sweep` - removes every entry whose `#write` call passed `stale: true`, leaving everything else.
5. Packer round-trip: when a `packer` is supplied (e.g. `Marshal`), every stored entry must be `packer.dump`'d when written, and `packer.load`'d when inspected — including `#read` and the `#sweep` stale check.

So for `packer: nil`, store the entry as-is in memory; with a real packer, store `packer.dump(entry)` and `load` it back before inspecting it.

**Critical subtleties:**
- Entries that have been removed by `#sweep` must *stay* removed even if `#sweep` is called again — so removal must be *deletion*, not merely marking `stale` as `true`. Otherwise `#sweep` would keep re-"removing" entries and `#read` would still find them.
- `#write` must also overwrite any entry previously removed by `#sweep` (a fresh write recreates the key), and must store the current `stale` flag (not preserve the old entry's flag).
- The "most recently written" entry under a key must be returned, so I can model that by re-storing under the same key (overwrite) — simplest correct model of "the entry most recently written under key."

```ruby
# A cache keyed by arbitrary keys. When constructed with a packer such as
# Marshal, every stored entry must round-trip through that packer
# (packer.dump on write, packer.load before any inspection, including #sweep's
# stale check). Without a packer, the entry is kept verbatim in memory.
class Cache
  # Entry must survive packer.dump/packer.load round-tripping (and Marshal in
  # particular), so it stays an immutable value object carrying the payload
  # and the `stale` flag captured from the #write call that created it.
  Entry = Struct.new(:payload, :stale)

  # Factory method (overrides Class#new) so constructing `Cache.new(...)` never
  # routes through an #initialize that isn't defined here.
  def Cache.new(packer: nil)
    allocate.tap do |cache|
      cache.instance_variable_set(:@packer, packer)
      cache.instance_variable_set(:@data, {})
    end
  end

  def write(key, payload, stale: false)
    entry = Entry.new(payload, stale)
    entry = @packer.dump(entry) if @packer
    @data[key] = entry
    entry
  end

  def read(key)
    return nil unless @data.key?(key)

    @packer ? @packer.load(@data[key]) : @data[key]
  end

  def sweep
    @data.keys.each do |key|
      entry = @data[key]
      @data.delete(key) if entry_stale?(entry)
    end
  end

  private

  def entry_stale?(entry)
    entry = @packer.load(entry) if @packer

    entry.stale
  end
end
```

```ruby
class Delivery

  end

  def log(tracking_id, status)
    @statuses[tracking_id] = status
  end

  def route(tracking_id, *args)
    status = @statuses[tracking_id]
    if block_given?

      block_return = block_return if args.size == 1
      block_return = block_return
    else

  end

    status = @statuses[tracking_id]
    if block_given?
      block_return = args[0].call(tracking_id, status) if args.size == 1
      block_return = block_return if args.size == 1
      block_return = block_return

      status

    if block_given?
      block_return
    else
      status
    end
  end
```

```ruby
class SparseArray
  include Enumerable

  def initialize
    @data = {}
  end

  def []=(index, value)
    raise TypeError, "index must be a non-negative integer" unless index.is_a?(Integer) && index >= 0
    @data[index] = value

  end

  def [](index)
    @data[index]
  end

  def each
    @data.keys.sort.each do |index|
      yield(index, @data[index])
    end
    self
  end

  def each_pair
    each { |k, v| yield(k, v) }
    self
  end

  def each_key
    each { |k, _v| yield(k) }
    self
  end

  def each_value
    each { |_k, v| yield(v) }
    self
  end

  def key_exists?(index)
    @data.key?(index)
  end

  def keys

  end

    else

    end

    else
```

```ruby
class TransientError < RuntimeError; end
class PermanentError < RuntimeError; end

module Retrier
  def self.call(max_attempts:, &block)
    attempt_number = 1

    loop do
      begin
        return block.call(attempt_number)
      rescue TransientError
        if attempt_number >= max_attempts
          raise
        end

        attempt_number += 1
      rescue PermanentError
        raise
      end
    end
  end
end
```

```ruby
class TokenStream
  def initialize(tokens)
    @tokens = tokens.dup
    @position = 0
  end

  def next
    raise StopIteration if @position >= @tokens.length
    token = @tokens[@position]
    @position += 1
    token
  end

  def peek
    raise StopIteration if @position >= @tokens.length
    @tokens[@position]
  end

  def rewind
    @position = 0
  end
end
```

```ruby
def parse(line)
  result = {}
  # Pattern to match key="value" tokens
  # Key can contain letters, digits, underscores (word characters)
  # Value can contain any characters except double-quote (greedy but careful approach needed)
  # We need to match key followed by ="value" where value doesn't contain "
  # But we must handle back-to-back pairs correctly
  
  # Use regex to find all key="value" patterns
  # Key pattern: word characters (or more specifically, keys in attrs usually are identifiers)
  # Value pattern: characters between opening and closing double quotes, allowing spaces
  
  line.scan(/(\w+)="([^"]*)"/) do |key, value|
    result[key.to_sym] = value
  end
  
  result
end
```

```ruby
class Weight
  include Comparable

  attr_reader :amount, :unit

  def initialize(amount, unit)
    @amount = amount
    @unit = unit
  end

  def ==(other)
    return false unless other.is_a?(Weight)
    @unit == other.unit && @amount == other.amount
  end

  def eql?(other)
    self == other
  end

  def hash
    [@amount, @unit].hash
  end

  def <=>(other)
    unless other.is_a?(Weight) && @unit == other.unit
      raise ArgumentError, "cannot compare Weights with different units"
    end
    @amount <=> other.amount
  end

  def clamp(*args)
    min = args[0]
    max = args[1]

    if min && min.is_a?(Weight)
      raise ArgumentError, "cannot clamp Weight with bounds of different units" unless @unit == min.unit
    end
    if max && max.is_a?(Weight)
      raise ArgumentError, "cannot clamp Weight with bounds of different units" unless @unit == max.unit
    end

    super
  end

  def between?(low, high)
    unless low.is_a?(Weight) && high.is_a?(Weight)
      raise ArgumentError, "cannot call between? on Weight without proper bounds"
    end

    raise ArgumentError, "cannot call between? on Weight with bounds of different units" unless @unit == low.unit && @unit == high.unit

    super
  end

  def to_s
    "#{@amount} #{@unit}"
  end

  def inspect
    "Weight.new(#{@amount.inspect}, #{@unit.inspect})"
  end
end
```

```ruby
class Counter
  attr_reader :value

  def initialize
    @value = 0
    @step = 1
  end

  def bump
    @value += @step
    self
  end

  def with_step(step)
    previous_step = @step
    @step = step
    begin
      yield
    ensure
      @step = previous_step
    end
    self
  end

  def dup
    copy = Counter.new
    copy.instance_variable_set(:@value, @value)
    copy.instance_variable_set(:@step, @step)
    copy
  end

  def clone
    copy = Counter.new
    copy.instance_variable_set(:@value, @value)
    copy.instance_variable_set(:@step, @step)
    copy
  end
end
```

```ruby
class Delivery

  end

  def log(tracking_id, status)
```

```ruby
class EventBroadcaster
  def initialize
    @listeners = []
  end

  def subscribe(listener)
    @listeners << listener
  end

  def publish(event)
    count = 0
    @listeners.each do |listener|
      listener.notify(event)
      count += 1
    end
    count
  end
end
```

message.content:
```ruby
class Retrier
  def self.call(max_attempts:, &block)
    attempt = 0

    loop do
      attempt += 1

      begin
        return block.call(attempt)
      rescue PermanentError => e
        raise e
      rescue TransientError => e
        raise e if attempt >= max_attempts
      end
    end
  end

  class PermanentError < StandardError; end
  class TransientError < StandardError; end
end
```

def Tally_group_by(items)
  result = {}
  items.each do |item|
    key = yield(item)
    if result.key?(key)
      result[key].push(item)
    else
      result[key] = [item]
    end
  end
  result
end

```ruby
class TokenStream
  def initialize(tokens)
    @tokens = tokens
    @position = 0
  end

  def next
    if @position >= @tokens.size
      raise StopIteration
    end
    token = @tokens[@position]
    @position += 1
    token
  end

  def peek
    if @position >= @tokens.size
      raise StopIteration
    end
    @tokens[@position]
  end

  def rewind
    @position = 0
  end
end
```

```ruby
class Interval
  attr_reader :start, :finish

  def initialize(start, finish)
    @start = start
    @finish = finish
  end

  def overlaps?(other)
    # Two intervals overlap if they share at least one point.
    # This includes intervals that only touch at a single shared endpoint.
    # Interval A: [start_a, finish_a]
    # Interval B: [start_b, finish_b]
    # They overlap if start_a <= finish_b AND start_b <= finish_a
    return false unless other.is_a?(Interval)

    # Check if there's any overlap, including touching endpoints
    !(self.finish < other.start || other.finish < self.start)
  end

  def to_a
    [start, finish]
  end
end
```
